# v0.28.0 — repeated compaction, slow summarisers: retry handling and turn preservation

The RELEASE-READINESS-V1 gauntlet at the `v0.28.0-rc1` tag passed, with the release-manager decisions disclosed below.
This tree is that tag plus this notes file.
Its receipts are attached to this release (see **Qualification**).

This minor release follows v0.27.0. It addresses repeated compaction, slow summary routes, and
stored-turn identity. Background leaf preparation slice 1 ships OFF. Local semantic recall remains
optional and OFF by default (FastEmbed is still installed separately); the managed deployment turns it
on per profile. There are no default changes in this release (#1151, #787, #1142, #1186).

## Upgrade

- **Host floor:** Hermes 0.21.3 or newer is required and 0.21.5 or newer recommended, both unchanged (#1080). Real-host
  CI now runs the plugin's real-host tests on the floor host (0.21.3), the managed runtime rung and Hermes 0.21.5 (#1235).
- **Dependency and store:** no new dependency and no schema change; rollback to v0.27.0 is plugin-only (#1151).
- **#1197 (#1198):** short non-empty user and assistant turns now receive embeddings under
  the conversational policy and the conversational half of heads. Tool rows and the full
  policy are unchanged; no new setting is introduced.
  With a local embedding provider (FastEmbed, or Ollama on a loopback host), existing stores fill the short-turn gap
  gradually, 32 items per session start or compaction, after new messages. With other providers (cloud, or Ollama on a
  remote host), chunks are not filled automatically, and `/lcm status` shows `(gap-fill)` until a complete manual run.
  To fill it sooner, run `/lcm embed backfill --corpus chunks --apply`. Add `--confirm-raw-text` for a cloud provider,
  and `--limit N` to raise the 200-chunk default per run. Repeat while `remaining` is above 0 and falling.
  On a synthetic 150,000-message store at v0.27.0's local state, a pre-rc dry run on main filled a 22,400-turn gap at
  67–98 turns per second; recall p90 stayed at 1.5–1.9 s (budget 8 s). The gauntlet receipt records the repeat at the `v0.28.0-rc1` tag.
- **Rollback:** target `v0.27.0`; plugin-only rollback does not replace the pending
  ordered-message and summary-DAG reader comparisons (#1104, #1245, #1285).

## Changes since v0.27.0

### Repeated compaction and slow summarisers
- **#787 (#1142):** background leaf preparation slice 1 prepares the next leaf after a turn
  and promotes it at the threshold only while the stored rows still match. It ships OFF.
- **#1122 (#1143):** pre-compaction extraction leaves the next summary call its estimated time.
- **#1137 (#1209):** a summary call that the foreground budget cuts after it ran at least 90% of its window opens that
  route's circuit (`hung`); an earlier cut keeps it closed. With a non-default summary timeout below the hard budget, a
  cut just short of that timeout opens the circuit at once, while a call that runs out the timeout counts as one of the
  two failures needed.
- **#1096 (#1329), #1369 (#1389):** the first sole-route hang, including one after a stored leaf or condensation in the
  same sweep, permits one retry at turn end; repeat hangs, including a forced-overflow retry that hangs again, retain
  the cooldown.
- **#1134, #1132, #1138 (#1212):** non-sweep admission uses the working leaf size;
  oversized indivisible leaves retry with the 8,000-token input clip. The default leaf target stays 2,000 tokens; ineffective ratio/minimum settings warn.
- **#1126 (#1144):** Codex long-context and Spark presets recommend 24,000-token chunks and drop the unimplemented
  low-water field; `/lcm preset show` displays each preset's recorded metrics or says none are recorded.
- **#1163 (#1172):** a valid nonce-tagged summary ending at its expand hint can omit the
  closing tag; tag-like tokens and reasoning headers still reject an unclosed reply.
- **#1127 (#1148), #1162 (#1218), #1180 and #1175 (#1205):** pre-leaf timing and
  compaction-stop causes are visible; survival-fit warnings distinguish failed summary chains
  from other fits without changing doctor status, and doctor pressure uses the gate's token estimate.
- **#1162 (#1178, #1182):** retained-occurrence stops name the blocking row and preserve
  the pressure-yield streak. Status counts zero-leaf selections; doctor warns after three.
  Capped assemblies keep an unsummarised newest visible reply in store order where possible without growing the input,
  even if that reply takes the view over the cap; when no placement passes its checks, the base view is kept and
  `reply_keep=residual` is logged.
- **#1193 (#1195), #671:** the optional stub-first exit target ratio defaults to zero, preserving
  existing behavior when unset. Applied targets appear in status and the stop line.

### Data integrity and session continuity
- **#1306 (#1401):** CLI `/new` rebinds the foreground engine to the new session. Host-contract
  documentation, real-host CI and the #1453 classification remain closeout obligations (#1439).
- **#1179 (#1406), #1328 (#1395):** fresh repeated user turns with distinct known timestamps or host identities are
  preserved instead of absorbed by an older equal-text occurrence. One case is still open: after a cold restart, an
  identical user message re-sent at the same position with a later timestamp is not stored as a new occurrence. The text
  survives once, at the old time (#1511, v0.29.0).
- **#1403 (#1418):** an unstamped stored copy needs canonical occurrence proof before a changed-prefix audit consumes
  it; without that proof (for example on hosts that emit no occurrence UIDs) the row is stored again, a possible
  duplicate rather than a loss. Existing unstamped windows can gain one copy per row on the first such audit, then none.
  An accepted compaction prefix survives the same ingest.
- **#1160 (#1424):** a busy session-end flush is retained and retried at later lifecycle
  boundaries and during bounded shutdown; warnings report the pending row count (#1210).
- **#1385 (#1400):** a replayed tool-output placeholder cannot borrow another row's stored
  evidence; ambiguous salvage preserves fresh content rather than claiming replay proof.
- **#1501 (#1504):** when Hermes rotates a session for compression and stores the next user turn at the replaced turn's
  stamp, a later replay at the turn's own stamp is recognized as the stored occurrence when recorded provenance proves
  it; uncertain cases and turns stored before this release keep a duplicate.
- **#1505 (#1516):** after a forced overflow recovery, a host that overwrites LCM-X's recovery row with the current user
  turn no longer gets that turn stored twice; every uncertain case still stores it (the T34 residual is #1508).
- **#1124 (#1146), #1141 (#1147), #1116 (#1117):** proven re-ingest copies do not consume
  leaf input, source-less leaves are refused before summary calls, and adopted stub-first exits
  write durable commit proof without doubling a carrier's summary prefix. Repeated tool
  groups stay whole, and user rows are never excluded by canonical copy evidence (#1154).
  These changes do not repair already wedged stores.
- **#1141 (#1185):** `/lcm rotate apply` is refused on Hermes, which reloads its own transcript; use
  `/compress here N` instead.
- **#773 (#1114):** uniquely proven salvage-cleared tool outputs replay their stored rows
  without copying later turns; ambiguous or fresh same-id outputs remain new content.
- **#1370 (#1398), #1201 (#1204):** standalone summary, recall and generated-context rows
  stay model-only on display-aware hosts; merged human text remains visible. Existing display
  rows are not rewritten. **#1281 (#1430):** keep the newest request whole
  when marking cannot meet the budget and the current list already fits.
- **#1330 (#1387):** embedding maintenance retires at session end and uses bounded exit waits.
  **#1476 (#1479):** a child compressor finishing after session end is not published.
- **#1157, #1291 (#1277):** bypassed child compression preserves the parent's status, stop reason and
  commit proof; each child keeps its own fallback compressor through lifecycle cleanup.
- **#1159, #1112 (#1173), #1396 (#1408):** store and DAG writes wait for competing writers;
  FTS checks retry schema errors once. Current assertion-store opens avoid DDL, and repairs
  of missing or outdated assertion objects are atomic.

### Recall and operator behavior
- **#1197 (#1198):** every non-empty conversational user/assistant turn receives a vector;
  existing stores gap-fill missing short turns (automatically with a local provider) and show `(gap-fill)` until done (see Upgrade).
- **#1194 (#1199):** empty optional array arguments behave like omitted arguments, preserving
  the documented answer-ready cursor behavior for `seen_refs: []`.
- **#1206 (#1207), #1255:** deadline reads retain pooled vector caches, and a handed-out
  vector store stays open until its query releases it.
- **#1090 (#1113):** replay prefix hashes stream once per reconciliation call and unused
  proof namespaces are skipped, preserving replay decisions with less repeated work.
- **#1161, #643, #574 (#1174):** indexed UID reads, early-exit session probes, evidence scans
  without a whole-corpus window, session-filtered retention queries and batched timestamp backfills reduce
  SQLite work while preserving query results.
- **#1261, #1267:** malformed boolean, integer and float values in the uniform `LCM_*` config loader, plus the named
  out-of-range, unknown-choice and dropped-item inputs, now warn through status and doctor; values stay unchanged.
  Standalone configuration wrappers load this plugin's module safely even after package eviction (#1261).
- **#896 (#1274):** doctor names stale chunk vectors in backfill guidance, with repeat and stop
  conditions. **#1246 (#1268):** enabling `LCM_CACHE_FRIENDLY_CONDENSATION_ENABLED` or
  `LCM_LARGE_OUTPUT_TRANSCRIPT_GC_ENABLED` warns; behavior stays unchanged until removal in v0.29.0.

  B sweep: PASS, 0 release-blocking defects. B hands-on: PASS;
  upgrade → v0.27.0 rollback → re-upgrade 6/6 PASS; host coverage 8 hosts, 0 product failures by the release-manager attribution ruling below: Hermes 0.21.5 tree (f97608f1); managed runtime at Hermes commits 99afd82c, 36a8f807, 7f76aff1 and 312f5baf; Hermes v0.21.7 (71d34bad, Python 3.14); Hermes v0.22.2 (d923a5eb); Hermes 0.21.3 (345cd2b0). Raw suite failures were 16 per host, 17 on the floor; all were attributed to tests and passed under their stated assumptions.
  C: PASS, 4 live host cells, 44 turns per cell, 72 committed compactions,
  0 lost rows, 0 duplicate rows, probes 10/12 exact, 2 recoverable, 0 LOSS, slowest compaction 116.009 s.
  Reference agent: 3 organic turns over 8.7 h, all answered; 0 lost rows,
  0 duplicate rows and 0 LCM-X tracebacks. This window qualifies integrity only.
  Latency is gated on controlled surfaces (see **Benchmark boundary**).

**Release-manager decisions.** Reference-agent window re-scope (integrity only; latency gated on controlled surfaces):
the window runs from the move AFTER line to the GA read and gates engine registration, zero LCM-frame tracebacks and publication-invariant lines, a clean doctor and completion of every organic turn; any compaction latency is reported only. Phase C, D2 wait reads, D7 and D5-B gate latency; there is no wall-clock soak wait. Track S D2 outcome: measured INCONCLUSIVE remains unchanged; waive the strict cp-304 mean bar with disclosure (0.775 vs v0.27.0 0.797), conditional on D7 facts ≥ 0.772 and all its other bars. D7 PASS on all six bars, facts 0.833, meets the condition; no facts-kept improvement is claimed. Phase C started under load: the pre-run decision accepted starting under load and running the last two cells together; PASS is accepted as conservative, while a latency FAIL would require an isolated re-run. The predeclared C3 identical-recipe re-measure replaces the entire first C3 row set after a canary was not sent; all three replacement probes were exact. C5 restart is PASS by ruling: two assistant fragments around a tool call join with no missing or duplicated content.
G3a under load: the release manager accepted running beside other gauntlet work under load; throughput is recorded only and a latency FAIL would require an isolated re-run. The fill finished early, so the concurrency bars use the 110 overlapping queries/ingests of 200 samples, as explicitly ruled. Host-suite attribution: raw full-suite failures were 16 per host and 17 on the floor, all in tests new in rc1; the release manager traced each group to a test assumption, each passed when re-run under it, and the gate counts 0 product failures; the four test fixes are tracked in #1539 (P4, v0.28.1). D4 QA scheduling: the predeclared one-reader-lane order was relaxed so candidate arms ran beside the baseline's last arm, and arms stopped by Codex transport errors were resumed under the same run ids and pins until complete; models, prompts, product trees, harness and scoring were unchanged and scores of incomplete arms were voided. The measured D4 PASS is separate from this decision.

## Known follow-ups
- **#1250:** a cold post-turn hook that carries no conversation identity still stores its rows under the session ID. A
  later bind to the real conversation does not re-own them, which can block summary publication and compaction for that
  session. No rows are lost on the current path, and the reference agent shows no new occurrences since 2026-09-24. The
  re-owning fix (open PR #1252) moved to v0.29.0: it stores these rows under a pending identity and re-owns them at the
  first bind, building on #1252.
- **#1186, #1197:** default-on, built-in local recall and background catch-up that re-queues itself are not in this
  release (#1186, v0.29.0); large-store ingest throughput and vector-search latency remain unproven; the merged
  short-turn fix is partial coverage.
- **#1096, #1097, #1141, #1162:** retry and diagnostic fixes do not recover every wedged
  session or resolve retained-occurrence escape; turn-end-free recovery remains follow-up work.
- **#1179, #1286, #1446, #1451, #1511:** retry-scaffold cold resume, stale proofs, occurrence snapshot
  durability/remapping and a user message re-sent at the same position after a cold restart remain open; the identity
  fixes above do not close those paths.
- **#1508:** after a forced overflow recovery and a crash before the reply, hosts without occurrence UIDs can store the
  next user turn twice on restart (a duplicate; nothing is lost). This is a regression from #1328 and depends on #849.
- **[#1529](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1529) (P2, v0.28.1):** on hosts that compact in place without message UIDs, a retried tool call whose result is the cleared-output placeholder can be dropped from the store (the call repeats a stored call and the result is placeholder text, so no user-written content is lost); v0.28.1 fixes the newest and second-newest cases. Its sibling with two or more following results is **[#1540](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1540) (P2, v0.29.0):** the pair is stored only at the next cold restart.
- **[#1536](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1536) (P2, v0.28.1):** after rollback to v0.27.0 and re-upgrade, short turns written during the rollback can miss embedding chunks and status under-reports the gap; v0.28.1 repairs stores stamped by v0.28.0.
- The background-review traceback on newer hosts is expected log output, not a failure ([#1439](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1439)).
- **[#1525](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1525) (P1, also in v0.27.0; fix deferred to v0.29.0):** after the host ingests a shortened list, new rows appended below the old length are not stored. A candidate fix was rejected in review because it introduced duplicates in other sequences.
  v0.27.0 behaves the same; which host paths do this is being established.
- **#1232:** name-only tool-result replay still needs occurrence proof. It remains a host
  prerequisite before the managed deployment adopts the affected host behavior.
- **#1149, #1388, #1397, #1399:** extraction deadlines, timing attribution and encoder/scheduler
  exit races remain follow-ups. **#1084, #1112:** CI mitigations do not establish flake causation.
- **#1111, #659, #1073, #1145:** pre-answer evidence, the carry packet and background
  preparation default decisions remain outside this release; no default change is claimed.
- P3 follow-ups from the release sweep: #1531, #1532, #1533.
- Test-only follow-up: [#1539](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1539) (P4, v0.28.1), four host-suite test fixes; 0 product failures on the 8-host set. This is not a known issue for users.
- The standing request and active constraints are kept only when the summariser quotes them (#659).

## Benchmark boundary
- The gauntlet ran at the `v0.28.0-rc1` tag. Its phase receipts (A–D) are linked above.
- Final-tag quality and large-store results are recorded in the Phase D scorecard. Earlier measurements do not
  establish this release's recall, facts kept, QA or latency results (#1197, #1315, #1128).
- Phase D at the rc1 tag: embeddings-OFF recall flips versus v0.27.0 PASS (0 flips;
  A/A′ 0 discordant rows and rankings over 100/100, aggregate metrics equal). Track S D2 INCONCLUSIVE (16.0 compactions per 100 messages,
  mean wait 6.14774 s, compaction p90 56.018 (including failed sweeps; successful-compaction p90 52.816) s, facts kept 0.775 vs v0.27.0 0.797 at cp-304 (−2.2 pt, exact stratified run-level permutation p 0.6019),
  0 (removed from live context by survival fits, not durable-store loss) rows dropped). QA PASS (LongMemEval-S 383 vs 380 of 500, LoCoMo 1,009 vs 1,007 of 1,986; no significant difference, 0 failed questions).
  Controlled-surface latency PASS (Phase C max 116.009 s ≤ 145 s; D2 wait-read p90/max 56.018/71.722 s ≤ 120/145 s; D7 p90 45.424 s ≤ 120 s and mean wait 7.5067 s ≤ 15 s; D5-B pooled p90/max 56.647/70.454 s ≤ 60/120 s across 39 attempts, with 33 committed events meeting the 10-event floor. The 60 s bound is a predeclared fallback, not a measured field percentile. Both D5-B cells stopped at turn 36 on provider quota; supporting integrity passed, recall probes were NOT REACHED (0 of 6 sent) and the close doctor was not reached).
  Short-turn gap-fill repeat PASS on the 150,000-message store with a 22,400-chunk gap: interruption/resume verified, final gap 0; resume 32.2 chunks/s (11,200 in 348 s), concurrent fill 48.2 chunks/s (11,277 in 234 s), under load. Recall p90 before/during/after 2.62/2.56/2.32 s against 8 s; the during value uses 110 concurrent queries. Concurrent ingest p90 2.02 ms, no increase against either idle baseline; allowed increase max(50 ms, 10%). Background preparation OFF/ON probe PASS / PASS on zero-gap and 60-second think-time stub-summariser probes, seeds 1–3: OFF worker construction/start/calls, enqueue and promotion activity all 0; ON one worker per seed, 36 worker calls per seed and pooled promotions 94/94 (rate 1.0) on each probe; rows and ordered identity preserved. Think-time visible-wait p90 OFF→ON by seed: 1.1691060830198694→0.9894989999884274 s, 2.9894639589765575→1.4394245410221629 s, 0.9543168749951292→1.0199914169788826 s; each arm has 28 post-crossing turns per seed. This measures ingest plus threshold compress to model dispatch, excluding response, preparation and think time;
  this probe records visible wait, while facts kept are recorded separately, and does not gate this release.
- The reference-agent window establishes integrity only this release. It does not establish latency.

Claim class: advisory release-note draft assembled from the named receipts. Does not prove final GA readiness, publication, customer-profile behaviour or reference-agent latency.
